models._description: Edit Attendee Details on Sales Confirmation
Edit Attendee Line on Sales Confirmation

behavioral_notes.observation: Confirming a sales order that carries any line whose product service_tracking == 'event' first raises ValidationError if any such line has no event_id, then calls order_line._init_registrations(): for each event line it creates (int(product_uom_qty) - len(existing registration_ids)) event.registration rows linked via sale_order_line_id/sale_order_id. Paid lines (price_total != 0) on a single-order confirmation are created in state 'draft' so attendee details can be captured before confirmation; free lines default to 'open' for seat checks. When confirming exactly one order the method returns the action_sale_order_event_registration act_window (the registration.editor attendee wizard) instead of the normal result. None of this SO->registration materialization is visible in metadata.

event.registration.create and write detect a sale_order_line_id in vals and call _synchronize_so_line_values(so_line), copying partner_id, event_id, event_slot_id, event_ticket_id and sale_order_id from the SO line onto the registration (public users are kept off the registration). On create, each SO-linked registration also message_post_with_source('mail.message_origin_link') to chatter-link the registration back to its sale.order. write() additionally detects a changed event_slot_id/event_ticket_id and fires _sale_order_registration_data_change_notify, which schedules a mail.mail_activity_data_warning activity on the sale.order rendering the event_registration_change_exception view. This bidirectional SO<->registration sync and the chatter/activity side-effects are pure code, not metadata.

A stored compute on sale_order_id.state / currency_id / amount_total drives both the new sale_status Selection (free / to_pay / sold) and the inherited registration state. If the order total is zero the registrations are 'free' and any draft/unset moves to 'open'; otherwise registrations on a confirmed ('sale') order become sale_status 'sold' and open, while not-yet-sold ones become 'to_pay' and fall back to 'draft'; registrations on a cancelled order are forced to state 'cancel'. _compute_field_value is overridden so that a registration transitioning draft/cancel -> open triggers _update_mail_schedulers (queues the event's after_sub attendee mails). So payment status on the sale order gates seat confirmation and attendee-mail scheduling.

For an event-ticket line _get_display_price returns the price taken from event.event.ticket (ticket.price, or ticket.price_reduce in the ticket's company currency when the pricelist hides discounts), converted to the SO line currency via _convert_to_sol_currency -- i.e. the ticket, not the product list price, sets the line unit price (_compute_price_unit is re-triggered on event_ticket_id). _get_sale_order_line_multiline_description_sale and event.event.ticket._get_ticket_multiline_description build the line label from the ticket (and slot) rather than the product, and product.template._onchange_type_event forces invoice_policy='order' for event service products. Ticket-based pricing/description override is not derivable from metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: sale.order.write partner sync + event.sale.report (_auto=False) + event.event.sale_price_total rollup
behavioral_notes.observation: sale.order.write propagates a changed partner_id down to all linked event.registration rows (sudo) so a customer change in the website_sale/backend flow re-owns the attendees. event.sale.report is an _auto=False SQL-view model joining event.registration to sale.order.line for revenue/seat analysis by event, ticket and salesperson (read-only, event manager only). event.event gains a sale_price_total Monetary computed by _read_group over confirmed (state='sale') SO lines on the event (converted to the event company currency at today's rate), exposing per-event ticketing revenue; action_view_linked_orders opens only those confirmed orders. These joins/aggregations live in SQL/Python, not metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: frontend (OWL/JS) -- SaleOrderLineProductField patch + event configurator form view
behavioral_notes.observation: 2 JS files, 1 XML template, no OWL components of its own; it registers the event_configurator_form view (a form.Controller subclass whose onRecordSaved closes the window returning {event_id, event_slot_id, event_ticket_id}) and patches @sale/js/sale_product_field SaleOrderLineProductField.prototype so that, when a line's product service_tracking === 'event', editing/selecting the product opens the event_sale.event_configurator_action dialog (the event.event.configurator wizard) to pick event/slot/ticket and writes the result back onto the SO line; cancelling clears the product. Asset bundles ['web.assets_backend','web.assets_tests'].

it_architecture.application: event_sale (Events Sales bridge application component over event + sale)
information_flows: side-effect: sale.order.action_confirm -> sale.order.line._init_registrations -> event.registration rows (draft for paid, open for free)
side-effect: sale.order.action_confirm (single order) -> registration.editor attendee wizard (action_sale_order_event_registration)
side-effect: event.registration.create -> _synchronize_so_line_values + mail.message_origin_link chatter back to sale.order
side-effect: sale.order.write(partner_id) -> propagate partner_id to linked event.registration
pricing: sale.order.line unit price/description for an event line sourced from event.event.ticket (price/price_reduce), not product list price
rollup: event.event.sale_price_total <- sum(confirmed sale.order.line.price_total) per event

capabilities: Sell Event Tickets via Sales Orders
Configure Event/Slot/Ticket on an Order Line (configurator wizard)
Auto-create & Sync Attendee Registrations from Confirmed Orders
Capture Attendee Details at Sales Confirmation (registration editor)
Price & Invoice Registrations (ticket-based pricing, invoice on order)
value_streams: Sell-to-Attend (the bridge): quote event-ticket line -> configure event/slot/ticket -> confirm order -> auto-create registrations -> capture attendee details -> payment gates 'sold'/open seats + attendee mails -> invoice
products: product.template (service_tracking='event' ticket products; invoice_policy forced to 'order')
policies: 1 record rule: multi-company scoping on event.sale.report
@api.constrains on sale.order.line: an event ticket line must carry event + ticket (+ slot when the event is multi-slot)
action_confirm blocks confirmation while any event line is missing its event_id
registration state/sale_status governed by sale.order state & amount (free->open, paid->draft until 'sale'->sold/open, cancelled->cancel)
sales_team.group_sale_salesman implies the event registration desk group (cross-app permission bridge)
metrics: event.sale.report (revenues, untaxed price, ticket price, seats by event/ticket/salesperson)

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: event_sale is THE BRIDGE between event (a value network: a mediation/membership platform that connects organizers and attendees around seat capacity) and sale (a value chain: quote-to-cash document flow). Its own added value is monetizing event registrations -- turning a seat in the network into a priced, confirmable, invoiceable sale.order.line, and turning a confirmed order back into event.registration rows whose state/sale_status (free/to_pay/sold) is gated by the order's payment. Because the economic logic it manages is still network logic (selling access/membership to a capacity-constrained event, ticket-based pricing, attendee provisioning) rather than transforming inputs into a physical good, it is classified network, consistent with the bridged event(network) record; the chain side is inherited from sale and is what this module plugs into rather than what it is. It is a primary, customer-facing activity (it directly produces sellable, revenue-bearing registrations). APQC 3.0 Market and Sell is the closest PCF home -- registering paying attendees to a marketed event is a sell motion (order capture + pricing + ticket configuration), matching the sale and event records' 3.0 placement. (Alternative considered: 'chain', justified by reuse of sale.order/line and invoice-on-order revenue; rejected because the module's distinctive behavior is network monetization / attendee mediation, not a transformation step -- the chain mechanics belong to sale, which this bridge extends.)

standard_capabilities: event service product (service_tracking='event') sold on a quotation/sales order line
event/slot/ticket configurator popup on the order line
ticket-based pricing (ticket.price / price_reduce) overriding product list price, invoice on order
auto-creation of one event.registration per sold unit on order confirmation
payment-gated registration status (free / to_pay / sold) and seat confirmation
event sales & revenue analysis (event.sale.report pivot/graph) and per-event sale_price_total
typical_fits: paid conferences/trainings where tickets are sold through quotations and invoiced
B2B bulk ticket purchase (one order line, qty N -> N attendees) with attendee details filled later
internal/back-office ticket sales by a salesperson (no website needed)
common_gaps: online/e-commerce ticket checkout and public registration UX (needs website_event_sale)
deferred-revenue / per-attendance invoicing policies beyond invoice-on-order
custom approval or pricing rules on ticket lines beyond pricelist/ticket price
no HTTP routes of its own -- all interaction is backend ORM/forms
